title: The margin note that took 358 years

probes.question: True or false: Fermat published his proof of the theorem during his lifetime.

image.alt: Page 61 of the 1670 edition of Diophantus Arithmetica, showing Pierre de Fermat's observation printed beneath problem VIII.

panels.text: About 1637, the mathematician Pierre de Fermat scribbles a claim in the margin of a book: no three positive whole numbers satisfy aⁿ + bⁿ = cⁿ when n is larger than 2.
He adds that he has a marvellous proof, but the margin is too small to hold it. He never writes it down.
For centuries, mathematicians try and fail. It becomes one of the most notable unsolved problems in mathematics.
The twist: in 1994, Andrew Wiles finally proves it, using mathematics Fermat could never have known. Many doubt that Fermat ever had a correct proof.
